CLAUDE.md: # Anime studio: faceless videos with Aoi
This folder makes a full YouTube video with an animated host, Aoi (a pixel-art anime hologram), and no camera.
Read CONTEXT.md for the five stages. Each stage has a contract in stages/.
## What lives where
- CONTEXT.md: the pipeline in one table (stage, command, file it makes, who checks it).
- studio: the one command. `./studio <stage> <video>`.
- stages/01-voice ... 05-render: one CONTRACT.md each (reads, makes, check).
- stages/template: the empty video folder that `./studio new` copies.
- kit/: what every video shares.
- kit/character/aoi: Aoi's sprites (base + mouth and eye parts), made by kit/gen.
- kit/player: the scene kit (kit.js) that draws any frame from a video's bundle.json.
- kit/voices/voices.json: voice presets. kit/audio: music bed and sound effects. kit/fonts.
- videos/<video>/: one folder per video. All of a video's work stays in its folder.
- tools/: the code behind each command.
## How to work a video
1. `./studio new <video>`. Ask Nick the brief questions (who it is for, shape, metaphor, voice). Write brief.md.
2. Write script.md in Aoi's voice (see the brief). Run each stage in order. Stop at each check for Nick.
3. Do not start a stage until the check on the stage before it passed.
4. Write the storyboard as text first. Fix timing in storyboard.txt, not in code.
5. Other languages: after the English storyboard is timed, translate (lang/<lang>/script.md, same sentences; strings.json),
then speak, transcribe and cues with `--lang`. See CONTEXT.md.
6. For a moment the kit cannot draw, write a `custom` beat in the video's scene.js. Move it into kit.js if a second video needs it.
## Rules
- Nick picks the title and the thumbnail. Do not upload or publish.
- Render with two workers at most. Do not open windows on Nick's screen (headless only).
- Keep Aoi's look: change kit/gen prompts and run kit/gen/prep.py, never edit sprites by hand.
CONTEXT.md: # The pipeline
One video = one folder in videos/. Five stages. Each stage reads the file before it, makes one main file,
and a person checks that file before the next stage runs. That check stops one bad take from becoming a bad video.
| Stage | Command | Reads | Makes | The check |
| 1 Voice | `./studio speak <v>` | brief.md, script.md | voice/voice.wav, voice/take.md | Nick listens to the whole take. A bad paragraph: `--redo N`. |
| 2 Words | `./studio transcribe <v>` | voice/voice.wav | words.json, mouth.json, words_check.md | Read words_check.md. Fix wrong names in script.md. |
| 3 Storyboard | `./studio cues <v>` | storyboard.txt, words.json | cues.md, bundle.json | Read cues.md (the timed storyboard) before any animation. |

| 4 Animation | `./studio stills <v>` then `./studio preview <v>` | bundle.json, scene.js, kit/ | stills/sheet_*.jpg | Claude reads the sheets and fixes overlaps. Nick watches the preview with sound. Notes go back to storyboard.txt. |
| 5 Render | `./studio render <v>` then `./studio notes <v>` | everything above | render/<v>.mp4, render/<v>_phone.mp4, description.md | Nick picks the title and the thumbnail. |
## Languages (English sets the timeline)
A video can have more languages (`languages: en, ja` in brief.md). English goes through stages 1 to 3 first.
Then each other language is fitted onto the English timeline: every beat starts at the same second in every
language, so the renders have the same length and the same frame for every beat, and you can swap languages at any moment.
| Step | Command | Makes | The check |
| Translate | Claude writes lang/ja/script.md (same paragraphs and sentences) and lang/ja/strings.json (on-screen text) | | Nick or a reader skims it |
| Voice | `./studio speak <v> --lang ja` | voice/ja/voice.wav, voice/ja/fit.md | fit.md: no beat over 1.25x. Shorten a line that is. |
| Words | `./studio transcribe <v> --lang ja` | words.ja.json, mouth.ja.json, words_check.ja.md | Fix a misread word with `{shown|spoken}` |
| Storyboard | `./studio cues <v>` | bundle.json (all languages), subs/en.srt, subs/ja.srt | |
| Render | `./studio render <v> --lang ja` | render/<v>.ja.mp4 | `./studio watch <v>`: swap languages while it plays |
Subtitles come from the voice's own timing, snapped to where each sound starts, so they land on the words.
Every voice gets a subtitle track in every language: the Japanese voice with English subtitles shows each English
sentence over the Japanese sentence it translates (subs/ja-voice.en.srt), in one or two lines.
Defaults (Nick, 2026-10-29): on-screen text and subtitles are English whatever the voice (anime with subs).
`--subs ja|off` and `--text ja` change that; `captions: off` in the brief turns subtitles off.
## Styles (the look around Aoi)
A style is one file in kit/styles/<id>.js: background, how Aoi appears (hologram, solid, sticker, framed),
cards, fonts, subtitles, section label and transitions. Aoi's sprites never change. Pick one with `style:` in brief.md.
A style can `extends` another and change only a few things, so new rounds branch from a pick.
| Command | Makes |
| `./studio styles <v> --round 2 --parent <id> --styles a,b,c` | Six frames per style from the live player, no render (seconds) |
| `./studio gallery <v>` | The sheet page: every round, numbered, with Play live (EN or JA) |
The kit also handles, for every style:
- Content fills the space beside Aoi (`regionOf`): titles, statements, lists, steps and files size themselves to it.
- `sides: 'alternate'` moves her to the other lower corner at each chapter (`aoi=corner-left` or `side=left` on a beat forces it).
- `poses: true`: when a content beat starts she turns toward it (present_l/r, point_l/r) for about 2 s, with her own lip sync.
Poses: kit/gen/gen_poses.py (edits of base.png on green, then mouths and blink), keyed and scaled in kit/gen/prep.py.
Where it came from: animation studios since about 1930. Voice first, an exposure sheet with every syllable
on a frame, a storyboard timed to the track (the Leica reel), pencil tests in the sweatbox, then ink and paint.
| Studio step | Here |
| Record the voices first | speak |
| Exposure sheet | words.json + mouth.json |
| Leica reel | cues.md |
| Pencil test | stills sheets |
| Sweatbox | preview |
| Ink and paint | render |

subs.t: Hi! I'm Aoi.
And this whole video came out
of one folder on Nick's computer.
My voice, my face, every screen you see.
All of it.
Want to see how it works?
Let's open the folder.
Up top, there's a file called CLAUDE.md.
That's the map.
It tells any AI what lives where.
Then there's the CONTEXT.md file.
It's the whole pipeline in one table.
Five stages,
one command for each, the file it makes,
and who checks it.
First, the voice.
Then every word gets timed.
Then a storyboard gets timed to those words.
Then comes the animation.
And last, the render.
And between every stage,
Nick checks the file before the next one runs.
That's the whole trick.
Take anything you do over and over.
Make each step a folder,
give each folder a short file,
and let the AI walk through them.
See you in the next one!
